11 A picture frame hangs from a string. The string is supported by a pin. The frame is in equilibrium.
string
pin
frame
Which diagram shows the vector triangle of forces acting on the picture frame?
A
B
C
D

hints: Notice the three forces on the frame itself: weight vertically down and two string tensions pulling up and inward from the left and right attachments.
For equilibrium the three force vectors must add to zero, so when placed head-to-tail they must form a closed triangle with arrows running continuously around it.
Check which triangle has the vertical side pointing down for weight and the other two sides pointing up-right and up-left to close the loop.
walkthrough: Identify the forces on the frame: weight $W$ vertically down, left-string tension $T_L$ pulling up and to the right toward the pin, and right-string tension $T_R$ pulling up and to the left toward the pin.
For coplanar equilibrium the vector sum is zero, so the three vectors placed head-to-tail must form a closed triangle.
Therefore the triangle must have one vertical side representing $W$ pointing down, and two slanted sides representing $T_L$ and $T_R$ pointing generally upward.

Eliminate any triangle where the vertical arrow points up, since that reverses the weight, and eliminate any triangle where two arrowheads meet or two tails meet at a vertex, since that is not head-to-tail.

Only one diagram has a downward vertical vector from top to bottom, then a vector from the bottom up to the right to the right vertex, then a vector from the right vertex back up to the starting top point.
This gives a continuous loop with zero resultant, matching $W + T_L + T_R = 0$. This is option D.

A.explanation: The vertical arrow points up and the arrows do not follow head-to-tail around the triangle, so it cannot represent weight acting down with closed equilibrium.

B.explanation: The arrows form a closed loop but the vertical arrow points up, whereas the only vertical force on the frame, its weight, must act down.

C.explanation: The vertical arrow correctly points down but two arrowheads point away from the top vertex, so the vectors do not join head-to-tail and do not sum to zero.

D.explanation: The vertical arrow points down for weight and the two slanted tension vectors join head-to-tail to close the triangle, giving zero resultant for equilibrium.
